scalars.scalar_value: This is a full-time career appointment, exempt (monthly paid) from overtime pay.
Experience supporting scientific research, laboratory, academic, accelerator, industrial controls, or other complex 24/7 operational environments.

Demonstrated people-management experience supervising technical staff, including assigning and reviewing work, setting priorities, coaching and developing employees, providing performance feedback, and addressing performance concerns.

items.item_text: Relevant cybersecurity certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, Security+, CASP+, SSCP, or comparable credentials.

This position is subject to a background check. Any convictions will be evaluated to determine if they directly relate to the responsibilities and requirements of the position. Having a conviction history will not automatically disqualify an applicant from being considered for employment.
Lawrence Berkeley National Lab, 1 Cyclotron Road, Berkeley, CA. A REAL ID or other acceptable form of identification is required to access Berkeley Lab sites (for more information ).

items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience, with a minimum of 12 years of relevant experience in a professional IT environment or 8 years with a Master’s degree.

Demonstrated people-management experience supervising technical staff, including assigning and reviewing work, setting priorities, coaching and developing employees, providing performance feedback, and addressing performance concerns.
Experience supporting scientific research, laboratory, academic, accelerator, industrial controls, or other complex 24/7 operational environments.
Proven experience leading cybersecurity initiatives and complex technical projects in enterprise or similarly complex IT environments, preferably within a research or academic setting.
Experience implementing Zero Trust principles in environments that include specialized, legacy, or operational technology systems.
In-depth knowledge of Windows and Linux systems and strong working knowledge of macOS, including experience administering and troubleshooting cross-platform computing environments.
Experience leading disaster recovery, business continuity, or cybersecurity tabletop exercises for mission-critical infrastructure.
Hands-on experience with Kubernetes, containerized application deployments, infrastructure automation, and CI/CD pipelines.
Experience with infrastructure-as-code, configuration management, observability, or enterprise automation technologies.
Experience administering enterprise storage systems, such as NetApp, with a strong understanding of RAID concepts, configurations, and levels.
Experience managing data center and server-room infrastructure, including rack layout, power distribution and management, cooling requirements, server hardware, and storage systems.
Broad knowledge of cybersecurity concepts, tools, methods, frameworks, and evolving threats, supported by hands-on experience or formal training in network and cybersecurity practices.

Demonstrated experience implementing defense-in-depth cybersecurity controls, including system hardening, firewalls, endpoint protection, vulnerability mitigation, intrusion detection/prevention, and other technical safeguards.
Experience managing IT budgets, technology procurement, vendor contracts, and lifecycle replacement schedules for enterprise hardware and infrastructure.
Lead and supervise the ALS Information Technology (ALS-IT) team, providing coaching, performance management, hiring, employee development, and oversight in accordance with Laboratory policies.

Set strategic and technical direction for the IT infrastructure supporting the Advanced Light Source, including systems, servers, storage, networking, virtualization, identity management, and cybersecurity.
Develop and execute the ALS-IT technology roadmap, establish priorities, manage resources, contribute to budget planning, and lead infrastructure modernization initiatives.

Serve as the primary technical advisor and cybersecurity expert for the ALS beamline and controls computing environment, ensuring the reliability, security, and availability of mission-critical research systems.

Oversee the design, implementation, and administration , implementation, and administration of enterprise Windows and Linux environments, Active Directory, virtualization platforms, Kubernetes-based services, identity and access management, and infrastructure automation.
Oversee system monitoring, incident response, patch management, disaster recovery, and operational support to maintain high availability for scientific operations.
Direct disaster recovery and business continuity planning, testing, and drills tailored to scientific data storage, control room systems, and other mission-critical user facility operations.
Partner with ALS leadership, beamline scientists, and Berkeley Lab IT to develop technology solutions, establish best practices, and support complex scientific computing initiatives.

Drive network security and infrastructure modernization initiatives, including the implementation of Zero Trust principles for edge devices and systems within the ALS beamline and controls computing environment.

Establish and maintain Service Level Agreements, support procedures, and ticketing workflows that provide responsive and consistent IT services to ALS staff, scientific personnel, and visiting facility users.

Support accelerator operations and scientific user programs by ensuring reliable IT services for the ALS Control Room, beamlines, and research operations, including occasional after-hours support during critical operational periods in support of ALS’s 24/7 operations.
Stay current with emerging technologies and recommend innovative solutions that improve operational efficiency, cybersecurity, and scientific computing capabilities.
Demonstrated familiarity with NIST SP 800-53 security controls, the DOE Risk Management Framework, or comparable federal cybersecurity standards and frameworks.
Broad and specialized expertise in enterprise systems administration and cybersecurity sufficient to serve as a trusted technical advisor and recognized subject-matter expert.
Strong commitment to promoting, implementing, and modeling effective cybersecurity practices while maintaining reliable, secure, and highly available IT services.
Demonstrated ability to work independently with minimal supervision, exercise sound technical judgment, and lead complex initiatives from planning through implementation.
In-depth knowledge of virtualized server environments and infrastructure, such as VMware, Hyper-V, or Proxmox.
Advanced knowledge of computer hardware, including PC and Mac workstations, rack-mounted server hardware, and networking and security devices.

Advanced knowledge of enterprise networking and network security, including TCP/IP, routing and switching, subnetted environments, remote-access technologies, and network troubleshooting using packet-analysis tools.

Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to work effectively with a wide variety of colleagues, explain complex technical information clearly and concisely, and produce well-crafted technical documentation.
